events.title: Atomic Bomb Dropped on Nagasaki
events.description: The United States detonated a plutonium implosion atomic bomb, nicknamed Fat Man, over the Japanese city of Nagasaki, three days after the bombing of Hiroshima. An estimated 40,000 people were killed instantly, with tens of thousands more dying by the end of the year.
events.significance: This was the second and last use of a nuclear weapon in warfare. It contributed to Japan's announcement of surrender on August 15, 1945, ending World War II, and shaped the global debate on nuclear weapons.

events.title: Richard Nixon's Resignation Takes Effect
events.description: Richard Nixon became the first U.S. president to resign from office, with his resignation taking effect at noon, a day after his televised address. Vice President Gerald Ford was sworn in as the 38th president.
events.significance: The resignation ended the Watergate scandal's impact on his presidency and tested the strength of American constitutional institutions, leaving a lasting effect on public trust in government.

events.title: Singapore Becomes an Independent Nation
events.description: Singapore was separated from Malaysia and became a fully independent sovereign republic, with Lee Kuan Yew as its first prime minister.
events.significance: The event marked the birth of Singapore as a nation, which grew from a small trading port into one of the world's leading financial and economic centers.

events.title: Quit India Movement Leaders Arrested
events.description: British authorities arrested Mahatma Gandhi and other Indian National Congress leaders in Bombay, a day after the Quit India resolution was passed, demanding an end to British rule in India.
events.significance: The movement intensified mass opposition to colonial rule and was an important step toward India's independence in 1947. August 9 is commemorated in India as August Kranti Day.

events.title: Jesse Owens Wins Fourth Gold Medal in Berlin
events.description: At the 1936 Berlin Olympics, American sprinter Jesse Owens won his fourth gold medal as part of the 4x100 meter relay team, after earlier winning the 100 meters, 200 meters, and long jump.
events.significance: Owens' achievements challenged Nazi racial ideology on a global stage and made him one of the most celebrated athletes in Olympic history.
